newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SAirGroup reveals flight operation loss.
newsitem.headline: SAirGroup reveals flight operation loss.

text.p: SAirGroup said Swissair's flight operations made a loss of around 120 million Swiss francs in 1996, but it hoped to make significant progress this year in cutting this deficit.
SAirGroup chief executive Philippe Bruggisser told a news conference that his target was still for Swissair's flight operations to become profitable by 1998.

"We hope to be able to significantly improve the airline's result (this year)," Bruggisser said, adding he hoped yields would only decline six percent in 1997 to 14 cents per revenue seat kilometre from 14.9 cents in 1996.
SAirGroup is budgeting for a 9.8 percent drop in its unit costs in 1997 to 9.2 cents per available seat kilometre with a target of seven cents in 1998.
SAirGroup has never officially published the result of Swissair's flight operations and the figure is not available in its annual or interim reports.
However, Bruggisser said reports of a loss of 280 million francs in 1996 were based on calculated costs of each route, which should be excluded to give a true result.
Firstly, a depreciation charge is calculated for each route even if the aircraft aleady is fully written off.
Secondly, capital costs are calculated that are higher than actual costs.
Thirdly, on-board duty free sales are not included in the calculated costs.
Fourthly, revenue from frequent flyer programmes are not included and fifthly, book gains for aircraft sales are not included.
